fun_highlights: The callback system is the single best anti-staleness lever. Cards like cb_books_late (D4: Calla re-reads the book at 50 after keeping it since 7), cb_first_loss (D6: Elias passes the token to a young hand at 67), and cb_lookaway (the 'stop this time for the person most would pass, a debt N years overdue') land with genuine weight because the specific age is inserted. These feel personal, not template.

Vocation arcs genuinely diverge. A soldier's adult band (service, ghost-at-3am, truth-to-the-young) reads nothing like a scholar's (question vs. paid work, guarding vs. giving the knowing). Across 15 dynasties the vocational fingerprints are visible: Saoirse (D1) and Mateo (D13 gen4) both soldiered, but the ghost-card in one and its absence in the other made them read as different people.

The generational dynasty layer — motto crystallisation, seat movement named in the life that caused it, heirloom callbacks — creates a real 'one more generation' pull. The Okonkwo 5-gen run (D4) building from 'a rented room' to 'an old and famous house' with 'We earn the bread we eat' coalescing across Noor's life was the most satisfying arc in the transcript. The seat-naming at death ('The family climbed in the world this generation') gives the player a clear scoreboard without stats.

Era colouring does meaningful work. The plague era's w_plague_tend card ('breathed the same close air as the dying because they should not die alone, and was lucky, and was changed') appears in D4-Elias, D6-Ingrid, D7-Otto, D14-Greta — same card, but the life context made each hit differently. The war cards similarly generate varied notes depending on whether the character is already a soldier.

Writing quality at the individual-sentence level is genuinely high. Phrases like 'the particular tiredness of the unanchored', 'the hungry years of study, begun at 22, at last came good', and the affair framing that varies by stats (spirit low = cold/self-aware; heart-led = self-deceiving) show craft. The freshPick pools are large enough that within a single life nearly nothing repeats verbatim.

The drifter arc (vocation='adrift') is a real structural alternative. The Okonkwo 3rd-gen Noor and Thorne's Vesna both drifted, but the midlife reckoning — 'make peace / grasp late for a single thing' — branched in opposite directions and their epitaphs diverged. This is a case where the engine's fifth life-shape actually works.
staleness: The 'Meet them halfway' / love-opening moment appeared as a distinct logged line in 26 of the roughly 60 individual lives in the transcript — nearly every life that wasn't cut short. The framing rotates across 7 variants (engine.js line 102) but the choice text is always identical and the logged outcome ('started building the days around another person', 'fell in love — the kind that quietly rearranges the furniture of a life') recurs verbatim across multiple lives. D4-Calla age 17, D6-Tomas age 20, D7-Caleb age 16, D9-Selma age 16, D13-Idris age 23, D14-Greta age 19 all record essentially the same beat within a short reading span. By dynasty 8 the pattern is reflexive.

The body-decline ambient observation pool fires four times per life (the _obsN cap) but the vit_tire and vit_neg pools are so large that the lines feel cosmetic rather than characterful — they carry no story weight. Across a long session, lines like 'The stairs have started to ask a question of them', 'The body has begun sending its small bills', 'The weather has begun living in their joints' accumulate as white noise. D13-Anders (age 74, 81) and D14-Anders (age 68) both fire vit body observations within a few years of each other; by the back half of the session the reader stops registering them.

The marriage prompt ('Ask. Build a life.' / 'Not yet. Maybe never.') is structurally visible in almost every long-lived adult life. Worse, the logged outcome lines have low variety despite large pools: 'Married [name] on an ordinary day, and meant every word of it' and 'Married [name] without ceremony and without a single doubt' appear verbatim in D9 (Selma) and D13 (Anders gen5), and semantically identical variants appear in D4, D6, D7, D11. The choice itself has no downstream callback — it is the most prominent beat with the least consequences attached.

The 'masterwork deferred' beat (m_maker_masterwork: 'kept the ordinary work coming and the lights on, and let the masterwork stay, as it always had, a thing they would make next year') appears at very similar life positions across D3-Cassian (age 54), D6-Cassian (age 55), D9-Emory (age 44), D13-Idris (age 57) — and in all four the same choice ('Keep the lights on instead') was taken and the same log line fires. The onceDyn:true cooldown is not being fully enforced here, or the pool of makers is dense enough that the cooldown window is shorter than the session.

The 'child question' prompt and log lines cluster: 'Had a child, [name]. The world rearranged itself around a small weight', 'Had a child, [name]. Was sure of nothing, that first night, except that it had happened', 'Had a child, [name] — and discovered a fear they had not known they owned' all appear multiple times in the transcript. D6-Tomas age 26, D7-Caleb age 35, D7-Otto age 33, D13-Idris age 32 all fire near-identical logged lines. The haveChild() pool has 8 base variants but the session's freshPick deduplication apparently doesn't extend across lives (only within them), so the same lines resurface every 4–6 lives.

The 'ancestor epitaph' recycling is visible at session scale despite the blocking logic. 'Gave away everything they knew, and so kept it' appears for D9-Selma and was intended for the teacher cluster; 'Was elsewhere as often as here, and the elsewhere was wide' fires for D10-Anders (gen1) and D14-Anders (gen2) in consecutive dynasties — that is a direct same-cluster, same-generation-spacing repetition that the recentC blocker should have caught, suggesting the cross-dynasty RECENT_CLUSTERS memory is not fully working as intended. 'Left more behind than they took, and the difference is what remains' also fires in D12 (Mira Halloran) and was echoed structurally in nearby lines.

improvements.what: Give the marriage beat a downstream consequence that varies by how you answered. A 'Not yet' that aged into a late marriage should gate a different tone at the marriage event (engine.js a_marry already does the late/early split), but a 'Not yet' should also set a flag that fires a midlife moment — cb_almost_married or a variant of m_old_flame — so the non-committer gets a distinct arc rather than the same beat arriving again unchanged.
improvements.why: The marriage prompt currently has no asymmetric consequence: both paths converge on the same domestic arc (marriage usually fires later anyway) or on near-identical solitude. It is the single most visible template beat in the transcript and the one most players make the same way. Making the 'Not yet' choice generate a different card cluster would visibly differentiate sessions.

improvements.what: Give the child log lines true cross-session deduplication. The haveChild() pool in engine.js uses freshPick(base, P), but freshPick's seen-set is per-life ('P' scope), not per-session ('S' scope). A separate S._usedChildLines set (analogous to the S._usedFurious flag mentioned in the code comments) would prevent 'The world rearranged itself around a small weight' from appearing in dynasties 6, 7, 9, and 13.
improvements.why: The child birth is the most mechanically frequent 'joy' beat across a long session. It fires in most long-lived adult lives. When its exact phrasing recurs every 4–5 lives the emotional reset it is supposed to provide is lost.

improvements.what: Throttle the love-opening 'Meet them halfway' visibility. The y_love1 prompt rotates 7 framings (rotI-based, line 102 of content.js) but all 7 have the same two choice texts. The logged outcome lines ('Fell in love — the kind that quietly rearranges the furniture of a life') are freshPick but per-life only. Apply the same cross-session freshPick memory here, and consider introducing 2–3 distinctly worded love-opening cards (one more guarded framing, one later-than-expected framing at youth ages too) to break the visual template.
improvements.why: The prompt appeared in a logged form in roughly 43% of all lives in the transcript. At that density it becomes background expectation rather than a moment.

improvements.what: The vit_tire / vit_neg ambient observation pools are correctly implemented but fire as filler rather than as characterful texture. Consider reducing the _obsN cap from 4 to 3, and adding a condition that at least one of the elder vit lines must be a CALLBACK to a specific earlier choice — e.g., if the character burned through reckless years (lived_reckless), one of the vit lines should explicitly reference the old speed ('The body is still billing for those years').
improvements.why: The body-decline observations currently have no relationship to the life that earned them. They read as ambient weather in every elder life regardless of history. One anchored callback among them would transform the whole pool from filler into resonance.

improvements.what: Tighten the onceDyn enforcement on m_maker_masterwork and e_craft so they cannot both appear in the same dynasty (currently the masterwork is onceDyn:true for the card but its default cooldown of 3 can still let it reappear when a maker-dense house runs 5 generations). Consider a shared onceDyn group so that whichever 'craft reckoning' fires first (masterwork, handoff, or regret) blocks the others for 4–5 generations.
improvements.why: The same deferred-masterwork beat landed in D3, D6, D9, and D13 at nearly the same life position (mid-50s), all with the same logged outcome. This is the clearest structural repetition in the transcript and would be caught by a grouped onceDyn guard.

verdict: A Life earns its genre and shows genuine craft: the callback system lands, the vocation arcs are structurally distinct, and individual sentences are often excellent. At dynasty 4–5 the game is genuinely moving. But a long session (15 dynasties) exposes a small cluster of very high-frequency beats — love-opening, child-birth log lines, marriage prompt, body-decline observations — that are not deduplicated across lives and collectively produce a recognisable template by the back half of the run. The staleness is not in the content (the pools are deep) but in the plumbing: per-life freshPick memory that resets each new life means the same lines resurface every 4–6 houses, and the reader stops arriving at them fresh. Fix cross-session deduplication on the 4–5 loudest recurring lines and add one consequential asymmetry to the marriage beat, and this becomes a genuine 7.5–8.0.
